causes.check: Unplug the peripheral and see whether it recovers; measure the board's 5V pin with a multimeter while the peripheral is working (below 4.5V is a problem)
causes.fix: Give the peripheral its own power supply with a common ground, or use a USB hub with its own power adapter

causes.cause: The Blue Pill's onboard 3V3 regulator can only supply about 300mA (less on some knockoff boards); a display plus sensors on the 3V3 pin exceeds it
causes.check: Are the peripherals on 3V3 or 5V?
causes.fix: Move anything that can run on 5V over to 5V; keep 3V3 for small sensors only

causes.cause: The USB cable is too thin or too long, causing a big voltage drop
causes.check: Try a shorter, thicker cable
causes.fix: Replace it

entries.explain: A USB port is a thin water pipe, and the board's 3V3 regulator is an even thinner pipe branching off it. Servos, displays, and LED strips are big buckets; filling them from a thin pipe will never work.
entries.ask_ai: My STM32 project has these peripherals: [list, with approximate current draw], all running off USB power. Please help me work out the current budget and give me a power plan (what goes on 5V, what goes on 3V3, what needs its own supply).

entries.symptom: I'm using two power sources (USB for the board, a battery for the motor) and the signals don't work at all

causes.cause: The two supplies' grounds aren't connected, so the board's "high" has no reference point for the peripheral
causes.check: Is there a wire between the two supplies' negative terminals?
causes.fix: Connect the two GNDs with a wire. GND only; never connect the positives

causes.cause: The grounds are connected but with a thin wire, and the motor's heavy current through it shifts the ground level
causes.check: Is the GND wire an ordinary jumper wire?
causes.fix: Use thick wire for the motor loop; join signal ground and power ground at the power supply (star grounding)

entries.explain: Two power supplies are like two towns at different elevations: "10 feet up" means a different height in each. Connect the ground of both towns (common ground) and heights finally have a shared reference.
entries.ask_ai: I'm powering my STM32 from USB and a [peripheral] from a [battery / adapter]. Please draw a text wiring diagram showing how GND should be connected, and explain why the positives must not be connected.

entries.symptom: My code won't run on the virtual board or throws an error, even though it looks fine
signals: works on the real board but not the simulator

causes.cause: The simulator only implements a subset of the Arduino API (pinMode/digitalWrite/delay/Serial.print and the like); advanced features (timer interrupts, direct HAL calls, DMA) aren't supported
causes.check: Check the simulator docs for its supported list, or strip the code down to a blink and see whether that runs
causes.fix: Stick to the supported subset while debugging; try advanced features on the real board

causes.cause: The code uses STM32-specific pin names or macros (PC13, LED_BUILTIN) the simulator doesn't recognize
causes.check: Does the error say some pin name is undefined?
causes.fix: Check which names the simulator accepts

causes.cause: Library dependencies: the simulator doesn't have the libraries in your lib_deps
causes.check: The error is No such file .h
causes.fix: Remove the library and get the core logic running first

entries.explain: The virtual board is a practice sandbox: it has roads and houses drawn in, but it never actually rains or gets windy. You can practice walking there, but not swimming.
entries.ask_ai: Running my STM32 code in [simulator name] gives [error]. The APIs my code uses are: [list]. Please tell me which of these probably aren't supported by the simulator, and how to split the code into a "simulatable" part and a "real board only" part.

entries.symptom: Everything works on the virtual board, but flashed to the real board it doesn't

causes.cause: The simulator doesn't simulate electrical problems: missing pull-ups, no common ground, weak power, 5V on a 3.3V pin. The real board exposes all of them
causes.check: Go back to the hardware sections and check the wiring item by item
causes.fix: Separate code problems from wiring problems: first flash a blink-only program to confirm the board is alive

causes.cause: The simulator's clock is ideal; on the real board, delay/millis depend on the clock configuration
causes.check: Is the blink timing right?
causes.fix: See millis_delay_weird

causes.cause: Simulated sensors return ideal values; real ones need warm-up time, delays, and sometimes return NaN
causes.check: Print the raw readings over serial and look at them
causes.fix: Add timeouts, retries, and sanity checks

entries.explain: The simulator is physics without friction; the real board is the world with friction. Getting the logic right is only step one. Power, wires, and timing are three things the simulator will never teach you.
entries.ask_ai: My code works in the simulator but on the real board [symptom]. Code: [paste]. Wiring: [describe]. Please list possible causes only from the angle of hardware factors the simulator doesn't model.

entries.symptom: Code from an AI fails to build because some pin name is not declared, or it uses names like D13 / A0

causes.cause: The AI defaulted to Arduino UNO and used D13/A0/13. In STM32duino, pins are named PA0, PB12, PC13, and so on
causes.check: Search the code for the first argument of every pinMode/digitalWrite/analogRead
causes.fix: Change them to the Pxn format. Tell the AI: "The board is an STM32F103C8T6 Blue Pill using STM32duino; use pin names like PA0/PC13"

causes.cause: The AI mixed HAL/CubeMX style (GPIO_PIN_13, GPIOC) with Arduino style
causes.check: Is there anything like HAL_GPIO_WritePin?
causes.fix: Use one style only; while learning, stick to Arduino style throughout

causes.cause: The AI assumed LED_BUILTIN is the onboard LED. On the Blue Pill in STM32duino it usually is PC13, but not in every configuration
causes.check: Writing PC13 directly is the safe bet
causes.fix: Hard-code PC13

entries.explain: Most of the Arduino code an AI has ever seen was written for the UNO, so unless you say otherwise it assumes you have one too. Start every question with your board model and framework, the way you'd tell a cab driver which city you're in.
entries.ask_ai: The board is an STM32F103C8T6 Blue Pill, PlatformIO + Arduino framework (STM32duino). Use pin names like PA0/PB12/PC13 everywhere; never D13/A0/bare numbers. The onboard LED is PC13 and is active-low. Please write [what you need].

entries.symptom: The AI told me to install a library pio can't find, or the library doesn't have the function it says it does

causes.cause: The AI invented a plausible-sounding library or function name that doesn't exist
causes.check: pio pkg search keyword, or search registry.platformio.org
causes.fix: Paste the search results back to the AI: "The registry only has these. Which one?"

causes.cause: The library is real, but the AI remembers an old API and the function was renamed in newer versions
causes.check: Open the .h files under .pio/libdeps/*/libraryname/ and search for the function name
causes.fix: Paste the header's function list to the AI and have it rewrite against the real API

causes.cause: The library is ESP32/AVR-only and won't work on STM32
causes.check: Check the Platforms tab on the library's page
causes.fix: Ask the AI for an alternative that lists ststm32 support

entries.explain: An AI writes code from memory, and the library and function names in that memory can be stitched together from pieces. Every library name it gives you has to be checked against the shelf, and the check is one command: pio pkg search.
entries.ask_ai: The library you recommended, [library name], can't be found in the PlatformIO registry. The output of `pio pkg search [keyword]` is: [paste]. Please pick one of these real libraries that supports the ststm32 platform, and only use functions that actually exist in its header files (if you're not sure, say so).

entries.symptom: I've made the changes the AI suggested three rounds in a row, the problem is still there, and it sounds certain every time

causes.cause: The AI is missing key information (the full error, the wiring, platformio.ini) and is guessing
causes.check: Look back at what you gave it. Did it include the complete error text, platformio.ini, a wiring list, and the board model?
causes.fix: Give it everything at once. Especially the error: paste the full original text, don't summarize it

causes.cause: The problem is actually hardware (wires, power, jumpers). The AI can only see code, so no amount of code changes will help
causes.check: Flash a minimal program that only blinks PC13. Does it blink? If not, it isn't a code problem
causes.fix: Use the minimal program to verify the hardware chain one link at a time (flash → reset → blink → serial), then come back to the feature code

causes.cause: You changed several things at once, so you can't tell which one helped or hurt
causes.check: Think back: how many things did you change last round?
causes.fix: One change per round, verify immediately, write down the result

entries.explain: An AI is like a mechanic who can only help you over the phone. If all you say is "it won't start," all they can do is guess. You have to describe every light on the dashboard and every sound. And some problems, like an empty gas tank, can't be fixed by working on the engine.
entries.ask_ai: We've tried [N] rounds without solving this. Before suggesting anything else, please list the information you would need to pin this down but that I haven't given you yet, and I'll fill it in one item at a time. What's known so far: board STM32F103C8T6 Blue Pill, PlatformIO + STM32duino, symptom [describe], full error [paste], platformio.ini [paste], wiring [describe].

entries.symptom: The AI or a tutorial says connect VCC/GND, but the part only shows VDD/VSS or other names

causes.cause: Same meaning, several spellings: VCC=VDD=V+=5V/3V3 (power +); GND=VSS=V-=0V (ground); SDA=DAT/D, SCL=CLK/C
causes.check: Match against the alias table
causes.fix: Wire by the alias; it is the same pin

causes.cause: Labels are on the other side or tiny next to the pins
causes.check: Flip it, add light, photograph and zoom
causes.fix: Send the photo to the AI and ask it to point at the pin

entries.explain: Like "restroom / bathroom / WC": different words, same door.
entries.ask_ai: My part has no VCC label, only VDD and VSS. Here is a photo, please map them for me.
